GEN.when: Written for Israel in the wilderness, around 1400s BC; covers creation to about 1800 BC
GEN.big: God creates a good world, people break it with sin, and God starts his rescue plan through one family: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
GEN.jesus: God promises a descendant of Eve who will crush the serpent (3:15) and a blessing for all nations through Abraham's offspring. Jesus is that offspring.

EXO.when: Egypt and the Sinai desert, around 1400s BC
EXO.big: God hears his people's cry, breaks Egypt's grip, brings them out, gives them his law and comes to live among them in the tabernacle.
EXO.jesus: The Passover lamb whose blood saves points to Jesus, "our Passover lamb" (1 Cor 5:7). The tabernacle shows God dwelling with people, which Jesus fulfills (John 1:14).

LEV.big: A holy God makes a way for sinful people to live near him through sacrifices, priests and a set-apart way of life.
LEV.jesus: Every sacrifice and the Day of Atonement point to Jesus, the final high priest and the once-for-all sacrifice (Hebrews 9-10).

NUM.when: The 40 years in the wilderness between Sinai and Canaan
NUM.big: Israel complains and rebels, and a whole generation dies in the desert, but God stays faithful and brings their children to the edge of the promised land.
NUM.jesus: Jesus compares himself to the bronze snake lifted up so people could look and live (John 3:14-15).

DEU.when: On the plains of Moab, just before Israel enters Canaan
DEU.big: Moses' farewell sermons: remember what God did, love him with everything, obey his word, and choose life.
DEU.jesus: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy to defeat Satan in the wilderness, and he is the prophet like Moses that God promised (18:15).

JOS.big: God keeps his promise and gives Israel the land as they trust him, fight, and divide it among the tribes.
JOS.jesus: Joshua's name is the Hebrew form of "Jesus" (the LORD saves); Jesus leads his people into the true rest (Hebrews 4).

JDG.when: Israel before the kings, about 1370-1050 BC
JDG.big: A downward spiral: Israel turns to idols, gets oppressed, cries out, God sends a judge to rescue, and they fall again. "Everyone did what was right in his own eyes."
JDG.jesus: Every flawed judge shows the need for a perfect rescuer and king.

RUT.when: During the time of the judges
RUT.big: A loyal Moabite widow and a kind Israelite redeemer show God's quiet faithfulness, leading to King David.
RUT.jesus: Boaz the kinsman-redeemer pictures Jesus, and Ruth is in Jesus' family line (Matthew 1:5).

1SA.who: Unknown, using records from Samuel, Nathan and Gad
1SA.when: Israel's shift from judges to kings, about 1100-1010 BC
1SA.big: Israel asks for a king like the nations. Saul starts strong and fails; God chooses David, a man after his own heart.
1SA.jesus: David, the shepherd king from Bethlehem, points to Jesus, the Son of David.

2SA.big: David's victories, God's covenant promising an eternal throne, then David's sin with Bathsheba and the family fallout.
2SA.jesus: God promises David a son whose kingdom will last forever (7:12-16), fulfilled in Jesus.

1KI.big: Solomon's wisdom and temple, then his heart drifts, the kingdom splits, and prophets like Elijah confront idolatrous kings.
1KI.jesus: Jesus is greater than Solomon (Matthew 12:42) and the true temple.

2KI.when: Elisha to the fall of Jerusalem, about 850-586 BC
2KI.big: Both kingdoms keep sinning despite the prophets; Assyria takes Israel and Babylon takes Judah.
2KI.jesus: Elisha's miracles foreshadow Jesus', and the surviving king at the end keeps David's line alive.

1CH.when: Written after the exile, retelling history from Adam to David
1CH.big: For returned exiles: you are still God's people. Genealogies, David's reign and preparation for worship.
1CH.jesus: The focus on David's line and the temple points to Jesus, the Son of David.

2CH.when: Written after the exile; Solomon to the exile
2CH.big: Judah's story told through its kings and temple worship: seeking God brings blessing, forsaking him brings ruin.
2CH.jesus: The book ends with permission to rebuild, a hope fully met in Jesus.

EZR.big: God moves a pagan king to send exiles home; they rebuild the temple, and Ezra calls them back to God's word.
EZR.jesus: God keeping his people and his promises after exile sets the stage for Jesus.

NEH.big: Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls in 52 days despite opposition, and the people recommit to God's law.
NEH.jesus: Nehemiah's leadership and prayer show the kind of godly leader fulfilled in Jesus.

EST.big: God is never named, yet he is clearly at work: Esther risks her life and the Jews are saved from genocide.
EST.jesus: Esther stands in the gap for her people at great risk, a shadow of Jesus' far greater rescue.

JOB.when: Set in the time of the patriarchs; date of writing uncertain
JOB.big: Why do good people suffer? Job loses everything, wrestles with God honestly, and finds that God himself, not an explanation, is the answer.
JOB.jesus: Job longs for a mediator and a living Redeemer (19:25). Jesus is the innocent sufferer who stands between us and God.

PSA.who: David and others (Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses)
PSA.when: Written over about 1,000 years, gathered after the exile
PSA.big: Israel's prayer and song book: praise, lament, thanks, confession and trust, for every season of life.
PSA.jesus: Jesus prayed the Psalms and fulfills them: the King of Psalm 2, the sufferer of Psalm 22, the Lord of Psalm 110.

PRO.big: Practical wisdom for daily life, built on one foundation: "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom."
PRO.jesus: Jesus is the wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:30), the perfect wise man.

ECC.big: Life "under the sun" without God is meaningless smoke. Enjoy God's gifts, fear him and keep his commands.
ECC.jesus: Jesus brings the meaning and resurrection hope that Ecclesiastes longs for.

SNG.big: A love poem celebrating the joy and commitment of love between a husband and wife.
SNG.jesus: Christians have long seen in it a picture of Christ's love for his bride, the church (Ephesians 5).

ISA.when: Jerusalem, about 740-680 BC, as Assyria threatened
ISA.big: God is the Holy One who judges sin, yet promises comfort, a suffering Servant and a new creation.
ISA.jesus: Isaiah is quoted all over the New Testament: the virgin birth (7:14), the child called Mighty God (9:6), the Servant pierced for our transgressions (53).

JER.big: The "weeping prophet" warns Judah for decades, watches Jerusalem fall, and announces a new covenant written on hearts.
JER.jesus: Jesus inaugurates the new covenant of Jeremiah 31 in his blood (Luke 22:20).

LAM.when: Just after Jerusalem's destruction in 586 BC
LAM.big: Five poems of grief over Jerusalem's fall, with hope in the middle: God's mercies are new every morning.
LAM.jesus: Jesus wept over Jerusalem and bore God's judgment so his people could be restored.

EZK.big: God's glory leaves the corrupt temple, judgment falls, but God promises new hearts, dry bones raised and his glory returning.
EZK.jesus: Jesus is the Good Shepherd Ezekiel promised (34) and the one who brings new hearts by the Spirit.

DAN.big: Faithfulness in a pagan culture, and visions showing God rules history and will give an everlasting kingdom to "one like a son of man."
DAN.jesus: Jesus called himself the Son of Man from Daniel 7 more than any other title.

HOS.big: God tells Hosea to marry an unfaithful wife and keep loving her, a living picture of God's relentless love for unfaithful Israel.
HOS.jesus: Jesus is the faithful husband who pays to bring his unfaithful bride home.

JOL.big: A locust plague is a warning of the coming Day of the LORD; return to God, and he will pour out his Spirit on all people.
JOL.jesus: Peter quotes Joel at Pentecost (Acts 2) when Jesus pours out the Spirit.

AMO.when: Northern Israel, about 760 BC, a time of wealth
AMO.big: God cares about justice: worship means nothing while the poor are crushed. "Let justice roll down like waters."
AMO.jesus: Amos ends with God rebuilding David's fallen tent, which Acts 15 applies to Jesus gathering the nations.

OBA.when: After an attack on Jerusalem, likely 586 BC
OBA.big: Edom gloated over Judah's fall, and God will judge pride; the kingdom will be the LORD's.
OBA.jesus: Jesus brings in the kingdom that belongs to the LORD.

JON.who: Unknown; about Jonah son of Amittai
JON.big: A prophet runs from God, is swallowed by a fish, and sulks when God shows mercy to Israel's enemies.
JON.jesus: Jesus points to "the sign of Jonah": three days and nights, then resurrection (Matthew 12:40).

MIC.big: Judgment on corruption, and hope of a ruler from Bethlehem. "Do justice, love mercy, walk humbly with your God."
MIC.jesus: Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem as the birthplace of the coming ruler: Jesus.

NAM.big: God will judge Nineveh, the cruel capital of Assyria.
NAM.jesus: God's justice against evil is fully dealt with at the cross and Jesus' return.

HAB.big: A prophet asks God hard questions about evil and learns to trust: "The righteous shall live by faith."
HAB.jesus: Paul builds the gospel on Habakkuk 2:4 (Romans 1:17).

ZEP.big: The Day of the LORD is near, but God will save a humble remnant and rejoice over them with singing.
ZEP.jesus: Jesus is the King in the midst of his people who removes judgment.

HAG.big: The returned exiles have neglected God's house; "consider your ways" and rebuild.
HAG.jesus: God promises to fill the house with glory and shake the nations, fulfilled when Jesus comes to the temple.

ZEC.big: Visions and promises to encourage the builders: God will return, and a humble King will come.
ZEC.jesus: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey (9:9) and is the pierced one (12:10) and the struck shepherd (13:7).

MAL.big: God confronts half-hearted worship, broken marriages and robbing God, and promises a messenger to prepare the way.
MAL.jesus: John the Baptist is the messenger, and Jesus is the Lord who suddenly comes to his temple (3:1).

MAT.who: Matthew (Levi), a former tax collector and one of the twelve apostles
MAT.when: Written around AD 60s for Jewish readers
MAT.big: Jesus is the promised Messiah, the King of the Jews, who fulfills the Old Testament and teaches what life in God's kingdom looks like.
MAT.jesus: Every chapter. Matthew keeps saying "this was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet."

MRK.who: John Mark, based on Peter's preaching
MRK.big: Fast-moving: Jesus is the Son of God who came "not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."
MRK.jesus: The whole book drives toward the cross and the empty tomb.

LUK.who: Luke, a doctor and Paul's companion
LUK.when: Around AD 60, carefully researched for Theophilus
LUK.big: An orderly account of Jesus, the Savior of the world, who seeks and saves the lost, outsiders, women, the poor and sinners.
LUK.jesus: Luke shows Jesus fulfilling "everything written about me in the Law, the Prophets and the Psalms" (24:44).

JHN.big: Written "so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name."
JHN.jesus: Jesus' "I am" sayings: bread of life, light of the world, good shepherd, the resurrection and the life, the way, truth and life.

ACT.big: The risen Jesus sends his Spirit, and the gospel spreads from Jerusalem to Judea, Samaria and the ends of the earth through Peter, Paul and ordinary believers.
ACT.jesus: Jesus keeps working from heaven through his Spirit and his church.

ROM.when: Written from Corinth around AD 57 to the church in Rome
ROM.big: The gospel explained: everyone has sinned, and God makes sinners right with him by grace through faith in Jesus, then transforms how they live.
ROM.jesus: Jesus is the center: "There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (8:1).

1CO.when: Written from Ephesus around AD 55 to a messy church in Corinth
1CO.big: Paul tackles division, sexual sin, lawsuits, worship and spiritual gifts, and points to love and the resurrection.
1CO.jesus: "Christ crucified" (1:23) and Christ risen (15) answer every problem.

2CO.when: Around AD 56, after a painful conflict with Corinth
2CO.big: Paul defends his ministry and shows that God's power shows up in weakness.
2CO.jesus: "God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God" (5:21).

GAL.when: Around AD 48-55, to churches in Galatia
GAL.big: Don't add law-keeping to the gospel; we are justified by faith in Christ and set free to walk by the Spirit.
GAL.jesus: "I have been crucified with Christ… Christ lives in me" (2:20).

EPH.big: Everything God has given us in Christ (chapters 1-3), and how to live it out (4-6): unity, new life, family and spiritual battle.
EPH.jesus: God's plan is to unite all things in Christ (1:10).

PHP.big: A thank-you letter full of joy in hard circumstances: "to live is Christ and to die is gain."
PHP.jesus: The hymn of 2:5-11: Jesus humbled himself to the cross and is exalted above every name.

COL.big: Jesus is supreme over everything, so you don't need anything added to him.
COL.jesus: "He is the image of the invisible God… in him all things hold together" (1:15-17).

1TH.when: From Corinth around AD 50-51, one of his earliest letters
1TH.big: Encouragement to a young persecuted church: keep growing, live holy, and have hope in Jesus' return.
1TH.jesus: The Lord himself will come down from heaven (4:16).

2TH.big: The Day of the Lord hasn't come yet; stand firm and keep working.
2TH.jesus: Jesus will return and overcome evil.

1TI.when: Around AD 62-64, to his young co-worker Timothy in Ephesus
1TI.big: How to lead a church: guard sound teaching, pray, appoint qualified leaders and fight the good fight.
1TI.jesus: "Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the worst" (1:15).

2TI.who: Paul, from prison shortly before his death
2TI.big: Paul's last letter: guard the gospel, endure hardship like a soldier, and preach the word.
2TI.jesus: "Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead" (2:8).

TIT.when: Around AD 63, to Titus in Crete
TIT.big: Appoint good leaders and teach believers to live godly lives because of God's grace.
TIT.jesus: "The grace of God has appeared… our great God and Savior Jesus Christ" (2:11-13).

PHM.big: Paul asks Philemon to welcome back his runaway slave Onesimus as a brother.
PHM.jesus: Paul offering to pay Onesimus's debt pictures what Jesus does for us.

HEB.when: Before AD 70, to Jewish Christians tempted to turn back
HEB.big: Jesus is better: better than angels, Moses, the priests and the sacrifices. So hold on and don't drift.
HEB.jesus: Jesus is the great high priest and the once-for-all sacrifice.

JAS.when: Around AD 45-50, one of the earliest New Testament books
JAS.big: Real faith shows up in real life: trials, speech, favoritism, money and humility.
JAS.jesus: James echoes Jesus' Sermon on the Mount throughout.

1PE.big: You have a living hope; live as holy strangers in this world and endure suffering like Jesus did.
1PE.jesus: "He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree" (2:24).

2PE.big: Grow in godliness, reject false teachers, and remember Jesus will return.
2PE.jesus: Peter was an eyewitness of Jesus' majesty (1:16).

1JN.big: How to know you have eternal life: believe in Jesus, obey his commands and love one another. "God is love."
1JN.jesus: "The blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin" (1:7).

2JN.big: Walk in truth and love, and don't welcome false teachers.
2JN.jesus: Confessing that Jesus came in the flesh is the test of truth.

3JN.big: Praise for Gaius's hospitality and a warning about Diotrephes.
3JN.jesus: Faithful believers support those who go out "for the sake of the Name."

JUD.big: Contend for the faith against false teachers, and keep yourselves in God's love.
JUD.jesus: "To him who is able to keep you from stumbling" (24).

REV.big: A vision of the risen Jesus, the battle behind history, God's judgment on evil, and the new heaven and new earth.
REV.jesus: Jesus is the Lamb who was slain, the King of kings, who says "I am making all things new."

GEN: God creates the heavens, the earth and everything in them in six days, makes people in his image, and calls it all very good.
God rests on the seventh day, forms Adam from dust, plants Eden, gives one command, and creates Eve as Adam's partner.
The serpent deceives Eve, Adam and Eve eat the forbidden fruit, sin and death enter, and God promises a coming victory over the serpent.
Cain murders his brother Abel out of jealousy, sin spreads through Cain's line, and Seth is born as a new hope.
The family line from Adam to Noah, with the refrain "and he died," broken by Enoch, who walked with God.
Humanity becomes violent and corrupt, God grieves and decides to send a flood, but Noah finds favor and builds an ark.
Noah, his family and the animals enter the ark, and the flood covers the earth for months.
God remembers Noah, the waters recede, Noah sends out birds, leaves the ark and offers a sacrifice.
God blesses Noah, makes a covenant never to flood the earth again with the rainbow as its sign, and Noah's drunkenness exposes his sons.
The table of nations: how Noah's sons Shem, Ham and Japheth spread out and became the peoples of the world.
People build the tower of Babel to make a name for themselves, God scatters them, and the line of Shem leads to Abram.
God calls Abram to leave home and promises land, offspring and blessing for all nations; Abram lies about Sarai in Egypt.
Abram and Lot separate, Lot chooses the land near Sodom, and God repeats his promise of land to Abram.
Abram rescues Lot from invading kings and is blessed by Melchizedek, priest-king of Salem.
God promises Abram descendants like the stars, Abram believes and it is counted as righteousness, and God seals a covenant.
Sarai gives Hagar to Abram, Hagar runs away pregnant, and God meets her as "the God who sees me"; Ishmael is born.
God renames Abram and Sarai as Abraham and Sarah, gives circumcision as the covenant sign, and promises Isaac.
Three visitors promise Sarah a son and she laughs; Abraham pleads with God to spare Sodom for the sake of the righteous.
Angels rescue Lot's family, Sodom and Gomorrah are destroyed, Lot's wife looks back, and Lot's daughters commit incest.
Abraham again passes Sarah off as his sister, this time to Abimelech, and God protects her.
Isaac is born as promised, Hagar and Ishmael are sent away but God cares for them, and Abraham makes a treaty at Beersheba.
God tests Abraham by asking him to sacrifice Isaac, then stops him and provides a ram: "The LORD will provide."
Sarah dies, and Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah as a burial place, his first piece of the promised land.
Abraham's servant prays for guidance and finds Rebekah as a wife for Isaac.
Abraham dies, Rebekah gives birth to twins, and Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew.
God renews the promise to Isaac, Isaac repeats his father's lie about his wife, and digs wells amid conflict.
Rebekah and Jacob deceive blind Isaac, and Jacob steals Esau's blessing; Esau vows to kill him.
Jacob flees, dreams of a stairway to heaven at Bethel, and God promises to be with him.
Jacob works seven years for Rachel, is tricked into marrying Leah, and works seven more; Leah begins having sons.
Rivalry between Leah and Rachel produces more sons, Rachel finally bears Joseph, and Jacob prospers with Laban's flocks.
Jacob secretly leaves Laban, Rachel steals the household gods, and Jacob and Laban make a peace covenant.
Jacob prepares to meet Esau in fear, wrestles with God through the night, and is renamed Israel.
Esau runs to embrace Jacob, the brothers reconcile, and Jacob settles near Shechem.
Dinah is violated by Shechem, and her brothers Simeon and Levi take brutal revenge on the city.
Jacob returns to Bethel and gets rid of foreign gods, God reaffirms his promise, Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, and Isaac dies.
The family line of Esau, the father of the Edomites.
Jacob favors Joseph, Joseph dreams of ruling his family, and his jealous brothers sell him into slavery.
Judah fails his daughter-in-law Tamar, she tricks him into fathering her twins, and Judah admits she was more righteous.
Joseph prospers in Potiphar's house, refuses the advances of Potiphar's wife, and is thrown in prison, but God is with him.
In prison Joseph interprets the dreams of Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker; the cupbearer forgets him.
Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams of seven good years and seven years of famine and is made second in command over Egypt.
Famine drives Joseph's brothers to Egypt; Joseph recognizes them, tests them and keeps Simeon.
The brothers return with Benjamin, and Joseph hosts them at a feast.
Joseph frames Benjamin with a silver cup, and Judah offers himself in Benjamin's place.
Joseph reveals himself and forgives his brothers: "It was not you who sent me here, but God."
Jacob takes his whole family to Egypt with God's promise to go with him, and is reunited with Joseph.
Jacob blesses Pharaoh, the family settles in Goshen, and Joseph manages Egypt through the famine.
Jacob blesses Joseph's sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, putting the younger ahead of the older.
Jacob blesses his twelve sons and promises that the scepter will not depart from Judah; Jacob dies.
Joseph buries Jacob, reassures his brothers that "you meant evil, but God meant it for good," and dies trusting God's promise.
EXO: Israel multiplies in Egypt, a new Pharaoh enslaves them, and the Hebrew midwives defy his order to kill baby boys.
Moses is saved in a basket, raised in Pharaoh's palace, kills an Egyptian, and flees to Midian; God hears Israel's groaning.
God speaks to Moses from a burning bush, reveals his name, "I AM WHO I AM," and sends him to free Israel.
Moses makes excuses, God gives him signs and Aaron as a spokesman, and Moses returns to Egypt.
Pharaoh refuses to let Israel go and makes their labor harder; the people turn on Moses.
God reaffirms his covenant promises to rescue and redeem Israel; the family line of Moses and Aaron.
Moses confronts Pharaoh, Aaron's staff becomes a snake, and the Nile turns to blood.
Plagues of frogs, gnats and flies; Pharaoh bargains and then hardens his heart.
Plagues on livestock, boils and hail, while God protects Israel; Pharaoh still refuses.
Plagues of locusts and darkness; Pharaoh drives Moses away.
God announces the final plague: the death of every firstborn in Egypt.
God institutes the Passover, the firstborn of Egypt die, and Israel leaves Egypt in the night.
God claims Israel's firstborn and leads the people by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.
Pharaoh pursues, God parts the Red Sea, Israel crosses on dry ground, and Egypt's army drowns.
Moses and Miriam sing of God's victory; at Marah God turns bitter water sweet.
The people grumble about food, and God provides manna and quail and teaches them to rest on the Sabbath.
God brings water from the rock, and Israel defeats Amalek while Moses' arms are held up.
Jethro visits and advises Moses to appoint leaders to share the load of judging the people.
At Mount Sinai God calls Israel to be his treasured possession, a kingdom of priests, and descends in fire and thunder.
God gives the Ten Commandments.
Laws about servants, violence and injury, including "eye for eye" limits on punishment.
Laws about property, restitution and caring for foreigners, widows and orphans.
Laws of justice, the Sabbath year and three yearly feasts; God promises an angel to lead them.
Israel agrees to the covenant, it is sealed with blood, and Moses goes up the mountain for forty days.
God gives instructions for the ark of the covenant, the table and the lampstand so he can dwell among his people.
Instructions for the tabernacle's curtains, frames and the veil separating the Most Holy Place.
Instructions for the bronze altar, the courtyard and oil for the lamp.
Instructions for the priests' garments, including the breastpiece bearing Israel's names.
Instructions for ordaining Aaron and his sons as priests and for daily offerings.
Instructions for the incense altar, the census tax, the bronze basin and the anointing oil.
God fills Bezalel with his Spirit to build the tabernacle and gives the Sabbath as a sign.
While Moses is on the mountain, the people make a golden calf; Moses intercedes and judgment falls.
God says he will not go with them; Moses pleads for God's presence and asks to see his glory.
God passes by Moses proclaiming his name, "merciful and gracious," renews the covenant, and Moses' face shines.
The people give generously and willing craftsmen begin the work.
The people give so much they must be told to stop; the tabernacle curtains and frames are made.
Bezalel makes the ark, table, lampstand and incense altar.
The altar, basin and courtyard are made, and the materials are counted.
The priests' garments are made exactly as commanded, and Moses blesses the work.
The tabernacle is set up and God's glory fills it.
LEV: Instructions for the burnt offering, given completely to God as a pleasing aroma.
Instructions for the grain offering.
Instructions for the peace offering, a shared meal of fellowship with God.
Instructions for the sin offering for unintentional sins by priests, leaders and people.
More on the sin offering and the guilt offering for specific wrongs.
Guilt offerings for wronging a neighbor, and rules for the priests about the offerings.
More rules for the guilt and peace offerings and the priests' share.
Moses ordains Aaron and his sons as priests.
Aaron offers the first sacrifices, and fire from God consumes them.
Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire and die; priests must treat God as holy.
Clean and unclean animals.
Purification after childbirth.
Diagnosing skin diseases and mildew.
Cleansing rituals for healed skin disease and for houses with mildew.
Uncleanness from bodily discharges.
The Day of Atonement: the high priest enters the Most Holy Place, and the scapegoat carries sins away.
Sacrifices must be brought to the tabernacle; life is in the blood.
Forbidden sexual practices; Israel must not live like the nations around them.
Be holy because God is holy: love your neighbor as yourself, care for the poor, deal honestly.
Penalties for idolatry, child sacrifice and sexual sin.
Holiness standards for priests.
Rules for eating holy offerings and acceptable sacrifices.
The appointed feasts: Sabbath, Passover, Firstfruits, Weeks, Trumpets, Day of Atonement and Booths.
The lamp and bread in the tabernacle, and a blasphemer is stoned.
The Sabbath year and the Year of Jubilee, when land returns and slaves go free.
Blessings for obedience, curses for disobedience, and God's promise to remember his covenant.
Rules for vows and dedications to God.
NUM: A census of Israel's fighting men, tribe by tribe.
The camp is arranged by tribe around the tabernacle.
The Levites are counted and assigned to serve at the tabernacle.
The duties of the Levite clans in moving the tabernacle.
Purity in the camp, restitution, and the test for a suspected unfaithful wife.
The Nazirite vow and the priestly blessing: "The LORD bless you and keep you."
The tribal leaders bring offerings to dedicate the altar.
The lampstand is set up and the Levites are dedicated.
Israel celebrates Passover, and the cloud guides when they move and when they stay.
Silver trumpets are made, and Israel sets out from Sinai.
The people complain about manna, God sends quail and judgment, and seventy elders receive the Spirit.
Miriam and Aaron oppose Moses, and Miriam is struck with a skin disease and then healed.
Twelve spies explore Canaan; ten bring a fearful report while Caleb urges them to go up.
The people rebel and want to return to Egypt; that generation is sentenced to forty years in the wilderness.
Laws about offerings and a reminder to wear tassels to remember God's commands.
Korah leads a rebellion against Moses and Aaron, and the earth swallows the rebels.
Aaron's staff buds, confirming God's choice of priests.
The duties and support of priests and Levites.
The red heifer ritual for cleansing from contact with death.
Miriam dies, Moses strikes the rock in anger and loses entry to Canaan, Edom refuses passage, and Aaron dies.
Bronze snake: the people are bitten for grumbling and healed by looking at a snake on a pole; victories over Sihon and Og.
Balak hires Balaam to curse Israel, and Balaam's donkey speaks.
Balaam tries to curse Israel but can only bless them.
Balaam's final oracle foresees a star rising from Jacob.
Israel joins in Moabite idolatry and immorality; Phinehas stops the plague with zeal.
A second census of the new generation.
Zelophehad's daughters win their inheritance, and Joshua is appointed to succeed Moses.
Daily, weekly and monthly offerings, and Passover offerings.
Offerings for the fall festivals.
Rules about keeping vows.
Israel takes vengeance on Midian, and the plunder is divided.
Reuben and Gad settle east of the Jordan after promising to fight for their brothers.
A record of Israel's journey from Egypt to the Jordan.
The borders of Canaan and the leaders who will divide the land.
Towns for the Levites and cities of refuge.
Daughters who inherit must marry within their tribe so land stays in the tribe.
DEU: Moses retells how Israel refused to enter the land out of fear.
The wilderness years and victory over Sihon.
Victory over Og, land given east of the Jordan, and Moses denied entry.
Obey God's laws, never make idols, and remember there is no other God.
Moses repeats the Ten Commandments.
The Shema: love the LORD your God with all your heart, soul and strength, and teach it to your children.
Israel is chosen not because they were great but because God loves them; drive out idolatry.
Remember the wilderness: man does not live by bread alone. Don't forget God when you prosper.
It's not because of your righteousness: remember the golden calf.
New tablets, and what God asks: fear him, walk in his ways, love and serve him.
Love and obey God; blessing and curse are set before you.

"Love is as strong as death… many waters cannot quench love."
ISA: God indicts rebellious Judah but invites them: "Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be white as snow."
In the last days nations will stream to God's mountain and beat swords into plowshares.
Judgment on Jerusalem's leaders and proud women.
The Branch of the LORD will be glorious, and Zion cleansed.
The song of the vineyard that produced bad grapes; woes on the wicked.
Isaiah sees the LORD high and lifted up, is cleansed, and says, "Here am I. Send me."
Ahaz is told to trust God; the sign of Immanuel, born of a virgin.
Assyria will come like a flood; trust God, not alliances.
"For to us a child is born… Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace."
God will use Assyria and then judge it for its arrogance; a remnant will return.
A shoot from Jesse's stump; the wolf will lie with the lamb.
A song of salvation: "With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation."
Judgment against Babylon.
Taunt against Babylon's king, "How you have fallen, morning star."
Oracle against Moab.
Moab's grief and a promised throne of justice.
Judgment on Damascus and Israel.
A message to Cush.
Judgment on Egypt, then a day when Egypt and Assyria will worship God.
Isaiah walks barefoot as a sign against trusting Egypt.
Babylon has fallen.
Judgment on Jerusalem's partying instead of repenting.
Oracle against Tyre.
God will judge the whole earth.
God will prepare a feast and swallow up death forever.
"You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you."
God will slay the dragon and restore his vineyard.
Woe to Ephraim's drunken leaders; God lays a precious cornerstone in Zion.
Woe to people who honor God with lips while their hearts are far away.
Don't rely on Egypt; "in returning and rest you shall be saved."
Woe to those who trust horses instead of the LORD.
A king will reign in righteousness.
God will be the stability of your times.
Judgment on the nations and Edom.
The desert will bloom, the blind will see and the redeemed will return singing.
Assyria's commander taunts Jerusalem.
Hezekiah prays and God destroys the Assyrian army.
Hezekiah's illness and recovery.
Hezekiah shows Babylon his treasures; exile is predicted.
"Comfort my people"; those who wait on the LORD will mount up with wings like eagles.
"Fear not, for I am with you."
The Servant who will not break a bruised reed and will bring justice to the nations.
"When you pass through the waters, I will be with you"; God is doing a new thing.
God pours out his Spirit; the foolishness of idols carved from firewood.
God calls Cyrus by name; "there is no other God."
Idols must be carried, but God carries his people.
Babylon will be humbled.
God refined Israel in the furnace of affliction for his own sake.
The Servant is a light to the nations; God won't forget his people.
The obedient Servant offers his back to those who strike him.
Look to the rock you were cut from; God's salvation lasts forever.
"How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news"; the Servant will be exalted.
The suffering Servant: "He was pierced for our transgressions… by his wounds we are healed."
Barren Zion will have many children; God's love will not be shaken.
"Come, everyone who thirsts"; God's word will not return empty.
Foreigners and outcasts are welcome in God's house of prayer.
God dwells with the contrite and lowly.
True fasting: loosen injustice, feed the hungry, and call the Sabbath a delight.
Sin separates us from God, so God himself comes as Redeemer.
"Arise, shine, for your light has come"; nations come to Zion.
"The Spirit of the Lord is on me… to proclaim good news to the poor." Jesus read this in Nazareth.
God will not rest until Zion shines; she will be called "My Delight."
The divine warrior; remembering God's past mercy.
"Oh that you would rend the heavens and come down"; we are the clay, you are the potter.
God will create new heavens and a new earth.
God looks to the humble; all nations will see his glory.
JER: God calls young Jeremiah: "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you."
Israel traded the fountain of living water for broken cisterns.
"Return, faithless Israel," like an unfaithful wife.
Disaster from the north is coming.
Not one honest person can be found in Jerusalem.
"Peace, peace," when there is no peace; ask for the ancient paths.
The temple sermon: the temple won't save you if you keep sinning.
The harvest is past and we are not saved; is there no balm in Gilead?
Jeremiah weeps; let him who boasts boast that he knows God.
Idols are scarecrows in a cucumber field; the LORD is the true God.
Judah broke the covenant; Jeremiah's own townspeople plot against him.
Why do the wicked prosper? God's answer.
The ruined linen belt pictures Judah's pride.
Drought, false prophets and Jeremiah's plea.
Jeremiah's complaint and God's promise to make him a fortified wall.
Jeremiah is told not to marry as a sign of coming disaster.
"The heart is deceitful above all things"; blessed is the man who trusts the LORD.
At the potter's house: God can reshape the nation.
The broken jar pictures Jerusalem's coming destruction.
Jeremiah is put in stocks; God's word is like fire shut up in his bones.
Zedekiah asks for help; God will fight against Jerusalem.
Judgment on Judah's kings.
God will raise up a righteous Branch; woe to false shepherds and prophets.
Good figs and bad figs: the exiles and those left behind.
Seventy years of exile in Babylon.
Jeremiah is put on trial for his temple sermon and spared.
Jeremiah wears a yoke: submit to Babylon.
The false prophet Hananiah breaks the yoke and dies.
Letter to the exiles: build houses, seek the city's welfare; "I know the plans I have for you."
God will restore Israel and Judah.
God promises a new covenant: "I will put my law within them… and remember their sin no more."
During the siege Jeremiah buys a field as a sign of future hope.
"Call to me and I will answer you"; the Branch of David will rule.
Judah breaks its promise to free slaves.
The faithful Rekabites shame unfaithful Judah.
King Jehoiakim burns Jeremiah's scroll, and it is rewritten.
Jeremiah is imprisoned.
Jeremiah is thrown into a muddy cistern and rescued by Ebed-Melek.
Jerusalem falls to Babylon.
Jeremiah is released and stays with Gedaliah.
Gedaliah is assassinated.
The remnant asks Jeremiah for guidance and is told not to go to Egypt.
They go to Egypt anyway and take Jeremiah.
Judgment on the Jews worshiping idols in Egypt.
A message to Baruch: don't seek great things for yourself.
Oracle against Egypt.
Oracle against the Philistines.
Oracle against Moab.
Oracles against Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, Hazor and Elam.
Babylon will fall and Israel will return.
More on Babylon's fall.
Jerusalem falls and King Jehoiachin is later released.
LAM: Jerusalem sits alone like a widow, mourning her destruction.
God's anger has fallen on Zion.
In deep suffering: "The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases… his mercies are new every morning."
A prayer: "Restore us to yourself, O LORD."
EZK: Ezekiel sees a vision of God's glory with living creatures and wheels.
God sends Ezekiel to rebellious Israel and has him eat a scroll.
Ezekiel is made a watchman for Israel.
Ezekiel acts out the siege of Jerusalem.
Ezekiel shaves his head as a sign of judgment.
Judgment on the mountains of idolatry.
The end has come.
Visions of idolatry in the temple.
Those who grieve over sin are marked and spared.
God's glory leaves the temple.
God promises to give a new heart and spirit.
Ezekiel acts out going into exile.
Against false prophets who say "peace."
Even Noah, Daniel and Job could save only themselves.
Jerusalem is a useless vine.
Jerusalem pictured as an unfaithful wife whom God still promises to restore.
Parable of two eagles and a vine; God will plant a tender shoot.
Each person is responsible for his own sin; "turn and live."
A lament for Israel's princes.
Israel's history of rebellion and God's patience for his name's sake.
God's sword of judgment.
Jerusalem's sins; God looked for someone to stand in the gap and found no one.
Two unfaithful sisters, Samaria and Jerusalem.
The siege begins and Ezekiel's wife dies.
Judgment on Ammon, Moab, Edom and Philistia.
Judgment on Tyre.
A lament for Tyre the merchant ship.
The proud king of Tyre falls.
Judgment on Egypt.
Lament for Egypt.
Egypt like a great cedar cut down.
A lament for Pharaoh.
Ezekiel the watchman; news that Jerusalem has fallen.
Against selfish shepherds; God himself will shepherd his flock.
Judgment on Edom.
God will give a new heart and put his Spirit within his people.
The valley of dry bones comes to life; Israel will be one nation.
Gog attacks God's people.
God defeats Gog.
A vision of a new temple.
The temple's inner rooms.
The priests' rooms.
God's glory returns to the temple.
Rules for priests in the new temple.
Land for the temple and the prince.
Offerings and worship.
A river flows from the temple and brings life wherever it goes.
The land is divided, and the city is named "The LORD Is There."
DAN: Daniel and his friends refuse the king's food and God gives them wisdom.
Daniel interprets Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a statue destroyed by a rock, God's coming kingdom.
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego refuse to bow and are protected in the fiery furnace.
Proud Nebuchadnezzar is humbled until he praises God.
Belshazzar sees the writing on the wall and Babylon falls.
Daniel keeps praying and God shuts the lions' mouths.
Four beasts, and one like a son of man given an everlasting kingdom.
Daniel's prayer of confession, and the seventy weeks.
Wars between kings of the north and south.
At the end, many will rise; the wise will shine like stars.
HOS: Hosea marries Gomer, and their children's names announce judgment.
Unfaithful Israel will be punished, then wooed back and betrothed to God forever.
Hosea buys back his unfaithful wife.
There is no knowledge of God in the land; my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.
"Come, let us return to the LORD"; God desires mercy, not sacrifice.
Israel is like a half-baked cake and a senseless dove.
They sow the wind and reap the whirlwind.
Break up your fallow ground; it is time to seek the LORD.
"When Israel was a child, I loved him… how can I give you up?"
Israel should return like Jacob did.
Israel's idolatry will bring death, yet God will ransom them from the grave.
"Return, O Israel"; God will heal and love them freely.
JOL: A locust plague devastates the land; call a sacred assembly.
"Return to me with all your heart"; God will restore the years the locusts ate and pour out his Spirit.
God will judge the nations and dwell in Zion.
AMO: Judgment on Judah and Israel for trampling the poor.
Because God chose Israel, he will punish them.
Israel did not return to God despite warnings; prepare to meet your God.
"Seek me and live… let justice roll down like waters."
Woe to those at ease in luxury.
Visions of locusts, fire and a plumb line; Amos is told to leave.
A basket of summer fruit; a famine of hearing God's word.
God will restore David's fallen tent.
OBA: Edom will be judged for gloating over Jerusalem's fall, and the kingdom will be the LORD's.
JON: Jonah runs from God, a storm hits, and he's thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish.
Jonah prays from inside the fish, and God has it spit him out.
Jonah preaches, and Nineveh repents and is spared.
Jonah is angry at God's mercy, and God questions his heart.
MIC: Woe to those who plot evil and steal land.
In the last days, nations will stream to God's house and beat swords into plowshares.
A ruler will come from Bethlehem.
"What does the LORD require of you? To do justice, love mercy and walk humbly with your God."
"Who is a God like you, who pardons sin… you will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea."
NAM: The LORD is slow to anger but will judge Nineveh; he is a refuge for those who trust him.
Woe to the city of blood.
HAB: Habakkuk asks why God allows injustice; God says he's raising up Babylon.
"The righteous shall live by his faith"; woes on the proud.
"Though the fig tree does not bud… yet I will rejoice in the LORD."
ZEP: The great Day of the LORD is near.
Seek the LORD, all you humble; judgment on the nations.
God will restore his people: "He will rejoice over you with singing."
HAG: "Is it time for you to live in paneled houses while my house lies in ruins?" The people resume building.
The new temple's glory will be greater; God will shake the nations.
ZEC: "Return to me and I will return to you"; vision of horsemen.
A man measures Jerusalem; God will be a wall of fire around it.
The high priest Joshua's filthy clothes are replaced; the Branch is coming.
"Not by might nor by power, but by my Spirit."
Visions of a flying scroll and a woman in a basket.
Four chariots; the Branch will be priest and king.
God wants justice and mercy, not empty fasting.
God will return to Zion, and many nations will seek him.
"Your king comes to you… humble and riding on a donkey."
God will care for his flock and gather them.
The good shepherd is rejected and valued at thirty pieces of silver.
They will look on the one they pierced and mourn.
A fountain to cleanse sin; strike the shepherd and the sheep will scatter.
The LORD will come and be king over all the earth.
MAL: God's love for Israel; priests offer blemished sacrifices.
Priests have failed; God hates divorce and unfaithfulness.
A messenger will prepare the way; "Will a man rob God?" Bring the whole tithe.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing; Elijah will come before the great day.
MAT: Jesus' family line from Abraham through David, and his birth to the virgin Mary: "God with us."
The wise men worship Jesus, Herod kills the boys of Bethlehem, and Joseph flees to Egypt.
John the Baptist prepares the way, and Jesus is baptized; "This is my beloved Son."
Jesus defeats Satan's temptations with Scripture, begins preaching and calls fishermen to follow him.
The Sermon on the Mount begins: the Beatitudes, salt and light, anger, lust, and "love your enemies."
Give, pray (the Lord's Prayer) and fast in secret; don't worry; "seek first the kingdom of God."
Don't judge; ask, seek, knock; the narrow gate; build your house on the rock.
Jesus heals a leper, a centurion's servant and many others, calms a storm and drives out demons.
Jesus forgives and heals a paralyzed man, calls Matthew, and raises a girl; "the harvest is plentiful."
Jesus sends out the twelve and warns of persecution: "Don't fear those who kill the body."
Jesus praises John and invites, "Come to me, all who are weary… and I will give you rest."
Lord of the Sabbath; Pharisees accuse him of working by Satan; the sign of Jonah.
Parables of the kingdom: the sower, weeds, mustard seed, yeast, hidden treasure and the pearl.
John the Baptist is beheaded, Jesus feeds 5,000 and walks on water; Peter sinks.
Real defilement comes from the heart; Jesus heals a Canaanite woman's daughter and feeds 4,000.
Peter confesses, "You are the Christ"; Jesus predicts his death: "Take up your cross and follow me."
The transfiguration; Jesus heals a boy; faith like a mustard seed.
Become like children; leave the 99 for the lost sheep; forgive seventy-seven times.
Marriage and divorce; the rich young ruler walks away; the first will be last.
Workers in the vineyard; "the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve."
Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey, clears the temple and tells parables against the leaders.
Parable of the wedding feast; give to Caesar what is Caesar's; the greatest commandment.
Seven woes against hypocritical religious leaders; Jesus weeps over Jerusalem.
Signs of the end and the temple's destruction; be ready, for no one knows the hour.
Parables of the ten virgins and the talents; the sheep and goats: "you did it to me."
Anointed at Bethany, the Last Supper, Gethsemane, betrayal and arrest; Peter denies Jesus.
Jesus is handed to Pilate, crucified and buried; Judas hangs himself.
The empty tomb: "He is risen." The Great Commission: go and make disciples of all nations.
MRK: John prepares the way; Jesus is baptized, calls disciples and heals many.
Jesus forgives a paralyzed man let down through a roof and calls Levi.
Jesus heals on the Sabbath, appoints the twelve, and his family thinks he's lost his mind.
The parable of the sower; Jesus calms the storm: "Who is this?"
Jesus frees a man from Legion, heals a bleeding woman and raises Jairus's daughter.
Rejected at Nazareth, he sends out the twelve, feeds 5,000 and walks on water.
Traditions versus God's commands; a Syrophoenician woman's faith; a deaf man healed.
Feeding 4,000; Peter confesses Jesus as Christ; "Take up your cross."
The transfiguration; "I believe, help my unbelief"; who is greatest.
Divorce, children, the rich man, and Jesus came "to give his life as a ransom for many"; blind Bartimaeus.
Triumphal entry, cursing the fig tree, clearing the temple.
Parable of the tenants; the greatest commandment; the widow's offering.
Signs of the end; stay awake.
Anointing at Bethany, the Last Supper, Gethsemane, arrest, trial and Peter's denial.
Jesus before Pilate, crucified; the centurion says, "Truly this man was the Son of God."
The tomb is empty; Jesus is risen.
LUK: Angel announcements to Zechariah and Mary; Mary's song; John the Baptist is born.
Jesus is born in Bethlehem, shepherds come, Simeon praises God, and the boy Jesus is in the temple.
John the Baptist preaches repentance; Jesus is baptized; his family line back to Adam.
Jesus is tempted, then reads Isaiah 61 in Nazareth: "Today this Scripture is fulfilled."
A miraculous catch of fish, healings, and the call of Levi.
Lord of the Sabbath; the twelve chosen; the Sermon on the Plain: love your enemies.
A centurion's faith, a widow's son raised, and a sinful woman forgiven who loves much.
The parable of the sower, calming the storm, Legion freed, a girl raised.
The twelve sent out, 5,000 fed, Peter's confession, the transfiguration; the cost of following.
Seventy-two sent out; the good Samaritan; Mary chooses the better part.
The Lord's Prayer; ask, seek, knock; woes to the Pharisees.
Don't fear people; the rich fool; don't worry; be ready.
Repent or perish; the narrow door; Jesus weeps over Jerusalem.
The great banquet; count the cost of being a disciple.
The lost sheep, the lost coin and the lost son: heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.
The shrewd manager; the rich man and Lazarus.
Forgiveness, faith, ten lepers healed (one returns to thank him), and the coming kingdom.
The persistent widow; the Pharisee and the tax collector; the rich ruler.
Zacchaeus: "The Son of Man came to seek and save the lost." Triumphal entry.
Jesus' authority is challenged; the parable of the tenants.
The widow's offering; signs of the end.
The Last Supper, Gethsemane, arrest and Peter's denial.
Trial and crucifixion; "Father, forgive them"; the thief: "Today you will be with me in paradise."
The empty tomb, the road to Emmaus, and Jesus appears to his disciples and ascends.
JHN: "In the beginning was the Word… and the Word became flesh." John points to the Lamb of God.
Water into wine at Cana; Jesus clears the temple.
Nicodemus must be born again; "For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son."
The Samaritan woman at the well finds living water; an official's son is healed.
A man lame 38 years is healed; Jesus claims equality with the Father.
Feeding 5,000, walking on water, "I am the bread of life"; many leave, and Peter says, "To whom shall we go?"
Jesus at the Feast of Booths: "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink."
A woman caught in adultery; "I am the light of the world"; "Before Abraham was, I am."
Jesus heals a man born blind: "I was blind, now I see."
"I am the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep."
Lazarus dies; "I am the resurrection and the life"; Jesus weeps and raises him.
Mary anoints Jesus, the triumphal entry, and "unless a grain of wheat falls to the ground and dies."
Jesus washes the disciples' feet; "love one another as I have loved you."
"I am the way, the truth and the life"; Jesus promises the Holy Spirit.
"I am the vine; you are the branches. Abide in me."
The Spirit will guide you into truth; "In the world you will have trouble, but take heart, I have overcome the world."
Jesus prays for himself, his disciples and all future believers.
Jesus is arrested, tried before Annas and Pilate; Peter denies him.
Jesus is crucified: "It is finished." He is buried.
Mary Magdalene meets the risen Jesus; Thomas doubts and then believes: "My Lord and my God."
Breakfast by the sea; Jesus restores Peter: "Do you love me? Feed my sheep."
ACT: Jesus promises the Spirit and ascends; Matthias replaces Judas.
The Spirit comes at Pentecost, Peter preaches, and 3,000 are saved; the church shares life together.
Peter heals a lame beggar and preaches.
Peter and John are arrested and boldly preach; the church prays and shares everything.
Ananias and Sapphira lie and die; the apostles are flogged and rejoice.
Seven men chosen to serve, including Stephen.
Stephen's speech and martyrdom; Saul approves.
Persecution scatters the church; Philip preaches in Samaria and to an Ethiopian official.
Saul meets Jesus on the road to Damascus and is converted; Peter raises Dorcas.
Peter's vision; Cornelius, a Gentile, and his household receive the Spirit.
The church accepts Gentiles; believers are first called Christians in Antioch.
James is killed, Peter is freed from prison by an angel, and Herod dies.
Paul and Barnabas are sent out on the first missionary journey.
They preach in Iconium, Lystra and Derbe; Paul is stoned and survives.
The Jerusalem Council decides Gentiles are saved by grace without circumcision.
Paul's second journey; Lydia believes; Paul and Silas sing in jail and the jailer is saved.
Paul in Thessalonica, Berea and Athens, preaching about the unknown God.
Paul in Corinth with Priscilla and Aquila; Apollos.
Revival in Ephesus and a riot over the goddess Artemis.
Paul's farewell to the Ephesian elders: "It is more blessed to give than to receive."
Paul goes to Jerusalem despite warnings and is arrested.
Paul tells his conversion story to the crowd.
Paul before the council; a plot to kill him; he's moved to Caesarea.
Paul before Governor Felix.
Paul appeals to Caesar.
Paul before King Agrippa: "Almost you persuade me."
Paul's voyage to Rome and shipwreck; everyone survives.
On Malta and in Rome, Paul preaches the kingdom of God boldly and without hindrance.
ROM: The gospel is God's power for salvation; humanity suppressed the truth and turned to idols.
Judging others while doing the same things; God judges impartially.
"All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God," and are justified freely by his grace through Jesus.
Abraham was made right by faith, not works.
Justified by faith, we have peace with God; while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
Dead to sin, alive to God; the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life.
The law shows sin, and the struggle: "the good I want to do, I don't do."
No condemnation in Christ; life by the Spirit; nothing can separate us from God's love.
God's sovereign choice and Paul's grief for Israel.
"If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord… you will be saved." How will they hear without a preacher?
God hasn't rejected Israel; Gentiles are grafted in.
Offer yourselves as living sacrifices; be transformed; love genuinely.
Submit to authorities; love fulfills the law.
Don't judge or trip up a weaker brother over disputable matters.
Welcome one another as Christ welcomed you; Paul's mission plans.
Greetings to many co-workers, men and women.
1CO: Divisions in the church; the message of the cross is foolishness to the world but God's power.
Paul preached Christ crucified, not clever words; the Spirit reveals God's wisdom.
The church is God's field and temple; Christ is the only foundation.
Servants of Christ; Paul as a father to the church.
Confront sexual sin in the church.
Lawsuits among believers; your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit; flee sexual immorality.
Food offered to idols; knowledge puffs up, love builds up.
Paul gives up his rights for the gospel; run to win the prize.
Israel's warnings; God provides a way out of temptation; do everything for God's glory.
Order in worship and the Lord's Supper.
Spiritual gifts; one body with many parts.
The love chapter: love is patient, love is kind… the greatest of these is love.
Prophecy and tongues in orderly worship.
Christ is risen, the firstfruits; death is swallowed up in victory.
The collection; "be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong."
2CO: The God of all comfort comforts us so we can comfort others.
Forgive and restore the repentant brother; we are the aroma of Christ.
The new covenant's glory; where the Spirit is, there is freedom.
Treasure in jars of clay; hard-pressed but not crushed.
A new creation in Christ; we are ambassadors of reconciliation.
Now is the day of salvation; don't be unequally yoked.
Generous giving, following Christ who became poor for us.
Paul defends his authority; take every thought captive.
A thorn in the flesh: "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness."
Examine yourselves; final warnings and greetings.
GAL: There is no other gospel; Paul's story of his call.
Paul confronts Peter; "I have been crucified with Christ."
We are justified by faith like Abraham; in Christ there is neither Jew nor Gentile.
No longer slaves but sons who cry "Abba, Father."
For freedom Christ set us free; walk by the Spirit and bear his fruit: love, joy, peace…
Carry each other's burdens; you reap what you sow; boast only in the cross.
EPH: Every spiritual blessing in Christ: chosen, adopted, redeemed and sealed by the Spirit.
Dead in sin, made alive by grace through faith; Jew and Gentile made one.
The mystery of the gospel for the nations; a prayer to know Christ's love.
Unity in the body; put off the old self and put on the new.
Walk in love and light; be filled with the Spirit; husbands, love your wives as Christ loved the church.
Children and parents, servants and masters; put on the full armor of God.
PHP: For me to live is Christ and to die is gain; live worthy of the gospel.
Have the mind of Christ, who humbled himself to the cross.
Everything is loss compared to knowing Christ; press on toward the goal.
Rejoice always; don't be anxious; "I can do all things through him who strengthens me."
COL: Christ is the image of the invisible God and supreme over all creation.
You are complete in Christ; don't be captured by empty philosophy or rules.
Set your minds on things above; put on love; rules for the household.
Devote yourselves to prayer; final greetings.
1TH: The Thessalonians turned from idols to serve the living God.
Paul's gentle and bold ministry among them.
Timothy brings good news of their faith.
Live holy lives; the Lord will return and the dead in Christ will rise.
The day of the Lord comes like a thief; rejoice always, pray continually, give thanks.
2TH: God will repay those who persecute you when Jesus is revealed.
The man of lawlessness must come first; stand firm.
Pray for us; if anyone won't work, he shouldn't eat.
1TI: Warning against false teaching; Christ came to save sinners, "of whom I am the worst."
Pray for everyone; one God and one mediator, Christ Jesus.
Train yourself for godliness; don't let anyone look down on you for being young.
Caring for widows and honoring elders.
Godliness with contentment is great gain; the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil; fight the good fight.
2TI: Don't be ashamed; God gave us a spirit of power, love and self-control.
Be strong in grace; endure like a soldier; rightly handle the word of truth.
Hard times will come; all Scripture is God-breathed.
Preach the word; "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race."
TIT: Teach sound doctrine; God's grace teaches us to say no to ungodliness.
Saved by God's mercy, not by our works; devote yourselves to doing good.
PHM: Paul asks Philemon to welcome back Onesimus as a brother in Christ.
HEB: God has spoken through his Son, who is greater than the angels.
Jesus was made like us to save us; don't drift away.
Jesus is greater than Moses; don't harden your hearts.
A Sabbath rest remains; the word of God is living and active; approach the throne of grace with confidence.
Jesus is a high priest who sympathizes with our weakness.
Grow to maturity; God's promise is an anchor for the soul.
Jesus is a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
Christ entered the true sanctuary with his own blood.
One sacrifice for all time; hold fast and don't give up meeting together.
The faith hall of fame: by faith Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses and many more.
Run the race with endurance, eyes fixed on Jesus; God disciplines those he loves.
Keep loving each other; Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.
JAS: Count trials as joy; ask God for wisdom; be doers of the word, not hearers only.
Don't show favoritism; faith without works is dead.
Tame the tongue; wisdom from above.
Submit to God, resist the devil; don't boast about tomorrow.
Warning to the rich; be patient; the prayer of a righteous man is powerful.
1PE: A living hope through Jesus' resurrection; be holy as God is holy.
You are a chosen people, living stones; Christ suffered for you, leaving an example.
Husbands and wives; always be ready to give a reason for your hope.
Suffer for doing good; love covers a multitude of sins.
Shepherd the flock; cast your anxieties on God; resist the devil.
2PE: God has given us everything we need for godliness; Scripture came from God.
The Lord isn't slow; he is patient, wanting all to repent; the day of the Lord will come.
1JN: If we confess our sins, he is faithful to forgive and cleanse us.
Jesus is our advocate; don't love the world.
See what great love the Father has given us that we are called children of God.
Test the spirits; God is love; perfect love casts out fear.
Whoever has the Son has life; you can know you have eternal life.
2JN: Walk in truth and love; don't welcome those who deny Christ came in the flesh.
3JN: Gaius is praised for hospitality; Diotrephes is rebuked.
JUD: Contend for the faith; keep yourselves in God's love; glory to the one able to keep you from stumbling.
REV: John sees the glorified Jesus among the lampstands: "I am the first and the last."
Letters to the churches in Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum and Thyatira.
Letters to Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea; "I stand at the door and knock."
The throne room of heaven: "Holy, holy, holy."
Only the Lamb who was slain is worthy to open the scroll.
The first six seals: the four horsemen.
The 144,000 sealed and a great multitude from every nation.
The seventh seal and the first four trumpets.
The fifth and sixth trumpets.
An angel with a little scroll.
Two witnesses; the kingdom of the world becomes the kingdom of our Lord.
The woman, the child and the dragon; they overcame by the blood of the Lamb.
The beast from the sea and the beast from the earth.
The Lamb on Mount Zion and the harvest of the earth.
The song of Moses and the Lamb.
The seven bowls of God's wrath.
The prostitute riding the beast.
Babylon the great has fallen.
The wedding supper of the Lamb; the King of kings rides out on a white horse.
Satan bound, the thousand years, and the final judgment.
A new heaven and new earth: God dwells with his people and wipes away every tear.
The river of life; "Behold, I am coming soon… Come, Lord Jesus."

missions: Tell your family what you're doing this year and why. Ask them to hold you to it.
Pray out loud with your wife, or a close brother if you're single. Short is fine.
At dinner, ask each person: "What's one thing you're thankful for today?"
Call your dad, or a man who's been like a father to you, and thank him for one specific thing.
Do one chore at home you normally leave to someone else, without being asked or mentioning it.
Pray over each of your kids by name before bed. If you don't have kids, pray for a family in your church by name.
Write your wife a note telling her one thing you respect about her. Hide it where she'll find it.
Turn the phone off at dinner every night this week. All of them.
Ask someone you've wronged to forgive you. Don't explain it away. Just own it.
Take one of your kids, or a young man in your life, out for breakfast. Ask about their life and listen.
Read one of this week's chapters out loud to your family.
Give something away that costs you. Money, time or a skill.
Ask your wife: "How can I pray for you this week?" Then actually pray for it every day.
Tell your kids a story about a time God came through for you.
Fast from something you lean on (a meal, social media, sports talk) for one day and pray in that time.
Encourage another man by text. Tell him specifically what you see God doing in him.
Get up 15 minutes before everyone else every day this week and spend it with God before your phone.
Bless your kids out loud before school or bed: "I'm proud of you. God has a plan for you."
Plan a date with your wife. You make every arrangement.
Ask your family: "Is there anything I do that makes it hard to talk to me?" Listen without defending yourself.
Serve someone outside your family this week: a neighbor, a widow, a single mom.
Memorize this week's verse together as a family.
Write down three ways God has provided for your family this year and share them at dinner.
Apologize to one of your kids for a time you got angry. Show them what humility looks like.
Invite a man who's alone to dinner or to watch the game with you.
Halfway. Tell your family one thing God has changed in you since you started.
Pray with your wife about one decision you're facing together.
Teach one of your kids or a younger man a skill you know. Use the time to talk about faith.
Go one full day without complaining. If you slip, start over.
Ask an older believer you respect for advice on one area of your life.
Write down your family's "why": what you want your home to stand for. Talk about it together.
Pay for someone's meal or groceries quietly.
Ask your kids what they think about God. Don't correct. Just listen and learn.
Take a prayer walk around your neighborhood and pray for each house you pass.
Thank your pastor or a church leader in person.
Read Ephesians 5:25-33 and ask your wife how you can love her better.
Have a screen-free evening with your family. Play a game, cook or go outside.
Pray for a man you don't get along with, every day this week.
Three-quarters done. Recommit out loud to your family to finish strong.
Share your faith story with someone who doesn't follow Jesus. Keep it simple and honest.
Ask your kids to pray for you, and tell them what to pray for.
Clean up something you've been putting off at home: a project, a room, a repair.
Send a handwritten thank-you to someone who has invested in your family.
Take your wife's or a friend's burden for a day. Find out what's weighing on them and carry part of it.
Choose a family verse and write it somewhere everyone sees it every day.
Talk with your family about how you spend money and what generosity looks like for you.
Check in on a man who has drifted from church or from God. Just ask how he's really doing.
Tell each person in your family one thing you love about them.
Plan how you'll keep reading after the 52 weeks are done.
Pray for your future grandkids and the generations after you.
Write a letter to your kids about what you learned this year. Keep it for them.
Finish. Celebrate with your family, and call out the next man to take the challenge.

talk.GEN: God made everything good. What's your favorite thing God made, and why?
talk.EXO: God rescued his people from slavery. What's something God has rescued our family from or helped us through?
talk.LEV: God told his people how to be close to him. What helps you feel close to God?
talk.NUM: Israel kept complaining in the desert. What do you complain about most, and what could we thank God for instead?
talk.DEU: Moses told the people to remember what God did. What's one thing God did for us we should never forget?
talk.JOS: God told Joshua to be strong and courageous. When do you need courage right now?
talk.JDG: People kept forgetting God and getting in trouble. What helps us remember God every day?
talk.RUT: Ruth stayed loyal to Naomi when it was hard. Who is someone you can be loyal to this week?
talk.1SA: God picked David because he looked at his heart, not his size. What does God see when he looks at your heart?
talk.2SA: David messed up big and told God he was sorry. Why is it important to admit when we're wrong?
talk.1KI: Solomon asked God for wisdom instead of money. If God offered you anything, what would you ask for?
talk.2KI: Some kings followed God and some didn't. What makes someone a good leader?
talk.1CH: David got everyone ready to worship God. What's your favorite way to worship God?
talk.2CH: When King Jehoshaphat was scared, he prayed and praised. What can we do when we're scared?
talk.EZR: The people came home and rebuilt God's house. What's something worth rebuilding in our family?
talk.NEH: Nehemiah prayed and then worked hard. What's something you need to pray about and then work on?
talk.EST: Esther was brave for her people. When is it hard to stand up for what's right?
talk.JOB: Job lost everything but still trusted God. How can we trust God when things go wrong?
talk.PSA: The Psalms are songs and prayers for every feeling. How are you feeling today, and can you tell God about it?
talk.PRO: Proverbs says wise people listen. Who gives you good advice?
talk.ECC: Life without God feels empty. What makes life truly good?
talk.SNG: God made marriage and love. What's something you've seen in a good marriage?
talk.ISA: Isaiah said Jesus would be called Prince of Peace. Where do you need peace?
talk.JER: God said, "I know the plans I have for you." What do you hope God has planned for you?
talk.LAM: Even when things were sad, God's love was new every morning. What's a new good thing from today?
talk.EZK: God promised to give his people a new heart. What would you like God to change in your heart?
talk.DAN: Daniel kept praying even when it was against the law. What would you keep doing for God no matter what?
talk.HOS: God kept loving his people even when they ran away. How does it feel to be loved even when you mess up?
talk.JOL: God said, "Come back to me with all your heart." What pulls our hearts away from God?
talk.AMO: God cares about people being treated fairly. How can we be fair and kind to others?
talk.OBA: God doesn't like it when we laugh at others' trouble. How should we treat someone who is struggling?
talk.JON: Jonah ran from God. Have you ever not wanted to do what God asked? What happened?
talk.MIC: God wants us to do what's right, be kind and walk humbly with him. Which one is hardest for you?
talk.NAM: God is patient but he also stops evil. Why is it good that God is fair?
talk.HAB: Habakkuk chose to be happy in God even when things were bad. How can we be joyful on a hard day?
talk.ZEP: The Bible says God sings over his people. How does it feel to know God delights in you?
talk.HAG: God told the people to put him first. What does putting God first look like for you this week?
talk.ZEC: Jesus came riding on a donkey, humble and gentle. What does it mean to be humble?
talk.MAL: God wants our best, not leftovers. What's something we can give God our best in?
talk.MAT: Jesus said to build your life on his words like a house on rock. What's one thing Jesus said that you want to live by?
talk.MRK: Jesus came to serve, not to be served. How can you serve someone in our family this week?
talk.LUK: Jesus came to find the lost, like a shepherd looking for one sheep. Why does God care so much about each person?
talk.JHN: Jesus said, "I am the light of the world." What does it mean that Jesus is our light?
talk.ACT: The first Christians were brave and shared Jesus with everyone. Who could you tell about Jesus?
talk.ROM: Nothing can separate us from God's love. What's something that makes you worry God might stop loving you?
talk.1CO: Love is patient and kind. Who is easy to love, and who is hard to love?
talk.2CO: God's power shows up when we're weak. When have you felt weak but God helped you?
talk.GAL: The Spirit grows love, joy and peace in us. Which fruit do you want more of?
talk.EPH: Paul says to put on God's armor. Which piece of armor do you need most today?
talk.PHP: Paul was joyful even in prison. How can we choose joy when things are hard?
talk.COL: Paul says to set our minds on things above. What do you think about most?
talk.1TH: Paul says to pray all the time. When during your day could you talk to God?
talk.2TH: Paul told them to keep working and not give up. What's something you're tempted to quit?
talk.1TI: Paul told young Timothy not to let anyone look down on him for being young. How can young people set an example?
talk.2TI: Paul said he finished the race. What does it mean to finish strong?
talk.TIT: God's grace teaches us to say no to wrong things. How can we help each other say no to wrong things?
talk.PHM: Paul asked Philemon to forgive and welcome back Onesimus. Is there someone you need to forgive?
talk.HEB: Hebrews lists heroes who trusted God. Who is a hero of faith you look up to?
talk.JAS: James says to be quick to listen and slow to speak. Who in our family needs us to listen better?
talk.1PE: Peter says to give your worries to God because he cares. What worry can you give to God tonight?
talk.2PE: Peter says to keep growing in faith. How have you grown this year?
talk.1JN: God is love. What's one way you saw love in our family today?
talk.2JN: John says to walk in love. What does walking in love look like at school or work?
talk.3JN: Gaius welcomed people into his home. How can our family make people feel welcome?
talk.JUD: Jude says God is able to keep us from falling. How does God help us stay strong?
talk.REV: Someday God will wipe away every tear. What are you looking forward to about heaven?

verses.text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.
Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
I can do all things through Christ, who strengthens me.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
Watch! Stand firm in the faith! Be courageous! Be strong! Let all that you do be done in love.
Finally, be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of his might. Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself up for me.

Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us, looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.
Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
Jesus said to him, I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, that no one would boast.

In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord, and not for men,
casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.

If it seems evil to you to serve Yahweh, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.
You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
that if you will confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.
Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the assembly, and gave himself up for it;

For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,
Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?
Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.
For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.

Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. Amen.
He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.

Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness, that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.
I press on toward the goal for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain, any more. The first things have passed away.
